description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/split.t's rows "assignment to split-to-array (pmtarget/package array)",
"(targ/lexical)" and "(stacked)" assert that
    @a = split ...;
writes the SAME array object rather than replacing it -- perl compiles the
split with the target array attached to the op (PMTARGET) and pushes straight
into it, so a reference taken BEFORE the split still sees the new contents.

PCL builds a fresh list and assigns, so `\@a` taken earlier still points at the
old contents.  It is the SV-identity family (NS:Scalar copy does not preserve
reference/SV identity) seen from the array side; it may also be a SPEED lever
worth measuring, since the copy is proportional to the field count.

The file's other causeless rows are perl-internals readouts (the B:: dump and
the compile-time/run-time re-eval counts).
subject: `my @a = split ...` : perl writes the array IN PLACE (the PMTARGET optimisation) and the rows assert it is the same array (op/split.t, 3 rows)
